hints: Include the constant of integration $+c$ to get $f(x) = 2x^3 + \frac{8}{x} + c$.
walkthrough:
Integrate the derivative function with respect to $x$:
$$f(x) = \int \left(6x^2 - 8x^{-2}\right) dx = \frac{6x^3}{3} - \frac{8x^{-1}}{-1} + c = 2x^3 + \frac{8}{x} + c$$

Substitute the known point $(2, 7)$ to determine the constant of integration $c$:
$$7 = 2(2^3) + \frac{8}{2} + c = 16 + 4 + c = 20 + c \implies c = 7 - 20 = -13$$

State the final equation of the function:
$$f(x) = 2x^3 + \frac{8}{x} - 13$$

ai_rubric.Finding a Curve from Its Derivatives: Integrates correctly to $2x^3 + \frac{8}{x} + c$ (B1). Substitutes $(2, 7)$ to find $c = -13$ (M1). States $f(x) = 2x^3 + \frac{8}{x} - 13$ (A1).
